To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a subcritical plasma can support an efficient acceleration of high energy electrons with a high charge if the pulse width matches the plasma wavelength and if the laser plasma parameters are tuned to the self trapping regime, where the laser beam radius does not change during propagation.

the charge of a relativistic laser pulse accelerated electron beam is maximized by a pulse width that is longer than both the laser wavelength and the pulse length, and the pulse radius remains unchanged during propagation in a subcritical plasm.

the charge of a relativistic high energy electron beam generated in a subcritical laser plasma can be increased to the multi nC range by using a laser pulse with a length longer than both the laser wavelength and the laser width.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a generation of an electron beam with a very high charge by a laser pulse propagating through a plasma.
the generation of high energy, high charge electron beams from a subcritical density laser plasma interaction.
the generation of a relativistic electron beam by a short laser pulse propagating along an underdense plasma channel.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the pulse width matching criterion is a necessary and sufficient condition for the self trapped relativistic channeling regime in a subcritical dense plasma.
the self trapped regime of relativistic self channeling in a subcritical dense plasma is the most efficient way to generate high energy high charge electron beams.

, in the case of an ultra intense laser propagating in a plasma, the laser pulse self trapping regime is always preferable for high energy particle acceleration, and the laser plasma parameters can be chosen to maximize the total particle charge.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a subcritical plasma is a very good medium for laser pulse self trapping, and a high charge electron beam is a very good source for the generation of secondary particles.

the laser pulse self trapping regime is a new regime in the laser plasma interaction and the high yield production of high energy particles is possible by the optimization of the laser plasma parameters.

we have shown that a high charge electron beam can be efficiently produced by an ultra intense short pulse laser propagating in a plasma, where the laser plasma parameters are optimized to produce relativistic channeling and the self trapping regime.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a high energy electron bunch can be generated with a high charge by a laser pulse propagating at a subcritical plasma density, if the pulse length is longer than both the laser pulse width and the plasma wavelength and if the pulse is self trapped.
the laser beam self focusing in a subcritical dense plasma is not only a mechanism to produce high charge electron beams but also an effective tool for controlling the laser beam propagation.
the pulse length is the key parameter to control the charge of a relativistic electron beam, which is quite opposite to the standard bubble regime.
